focal_region.annotated_sentence_text:
[Turn 1 USER]
e001	Our small academic software group has built an open tool for exploring archival text collections.
e002	It is not used for medical or individual decisions; it helps researchers find patterns and passages to inspect.
e003	Two labs have used private builds and want us to release a public beta.
e004	The analysis engine is stable on our test collections, but installation is awkward and the documentation assumes people understand our data format.
e005	Half the team wants feedback now.
e006	The maintainers worry a messy release will define our reputation.
[Turn 1 ASSISTANT]
e007	The decision depends on what you want the beta to learn and which failures would be informative rather than merely predictable.
e008	If most early users will fail at installation or formatting, the feedback may tell you what you already know and consume goodwill.
e009	If the private labs have only used familiar collections, a broader beta could reveal important assumptions.
e010	You might delay “public” while expanding a structured preview to users with different data.
[Turn 7 USER]
e057	I am leaning toward releasing an openly downloadable “workshop preview” with a fixed end date, office hours, and no compatibility promise, then deciding on the public beta after we review installation failures and the maintainer returns.
e058	I dislike inventing another label, and I know people can keep downloaded software after the date.
e059	But I also do not want to call it a public beta when our support capacity changes halfway through.
e060	I have not resolved whether citations should be allowed to reference the preview.
[Turn 7 ASSISTANT]
e061	The proposal makes the support window and decision point concrete, but your discomfort is justified: a new label cannot fully control how released software is used.
e062	Citation is the unresolved commitment because it can turn a temporary preview into a durable scholarly object.
e063	You could provide a citable project description without presenting the preview interface as stable, but researchers may still cite the software version they used.
e064	The plan can bound your promise; it cannot make public use temporary in every practical sense.
